items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: An athlete, a ball player, Ted Williams — he could hit so well so old. He kept those reflexes up.

ctx.x: In other words you’d be a subcontractor.

Yeah, that’s what I’d do yeah. But I would show him how the hand moves when you play time, show him how to define that. And that’s it. I wouldn’t bother with too much else. I wouldn’t bother with the reading, because you play better like this, off your reflex. See reflexes. Without the reflexes, better you sell shoes, really. You’ve got to have those reflexes. An athlete, a ball player, Ted Williams — he could hit so well so old. He kept those reflexes up. Yeah. He hit a higher average than any old guy that ever…
Oh that’s right, I read that. The only guy in history.
